title: Spike an IV bag and prime its drip chamber
instruction: Prepare the IV set aseptically: hold the saline bag by its hanger tab, remove the blue spike-port cap and the navy giving-set spike cap by their tabs without touching either exposed sterile interface, seat the spike to its collar, keep the chamber axis within 12 degrees of horizontal and its lower region below the port, then squeeze and release until the marked axial liquid length is 15-27 mm. Release everything and return both arms to their starting poses.
context: Spiking an IV bag and setting the drip-chamber liquid level are routine preparation steps performed by nurses and infusion technicians. The task tests coordinated stabilization, cap removal, axial insertion and controlled priming.
setup: Fixed YAM station; metres from the arm-base midpoint, x forward, y left. A nonsterile 34 x 54 x 0.4 cm stainless work tray covers x 0.16-0.50, y -0.30-0.24. A sealed 500 mL PVC saline bag lies at (0.32,0.06): 13 x 20 x 2.6 cm external pillow (676 mL bounding volume), 530 g filled mass, welded rim, 28 x 8 x 20 mm upright hanger tab, and two downward-side ports. Its 10 mm-diameter, 30 mm spike port has a blue 15 x 13 mm pull-off protective cap with a 10 x 10 x 20 mm tab. A sterile giving set is presented at (0.42,-0.13) in a fixed 55 x 110 x 14 mm white molded cradle that contacts only the capped chamber and tubing. A shallow 21 mm-wide channel supports the lower half of the 20 mm chamber; two 6 x 3 x 6 mm front bumps, one 40 x 4 x 6 mm rear stop and a 1 N molded snap retainer resist the 0.15 N cap-pull reaction. The snap releases under upward arm pickup, leaving the chamber crown accessible for vertical lift. The set has a 25 mm spike covered by a navy 18 x 10 mm pull-off cap with a 10 x 10 x 14 mm tab, a 20 mm-diameter x 45 mm clear chamber with a 39 mm graduated axial span, 10 cm tube and closed roller clamp. The capped spike and sealed bag port are sterile interfaces; after either cap is removed, neither exposed interface may contact a gripper or the work tray. During priming the chamber axis must remain within 12 degrees of horizontal and its lower region at least 10 mm below the port; measure liquid length along the graduated chamber axis from its outlet end.
scoring: Contamination latches 0: before spike lock, either exposed interface comes within 7 mm of a gripper TCP, or the open port/spike surface reaches within 0.5 mm of the nonsterile tray. Overfill above 34 mm also latches 0. Otherwise, measured at trial end: 0.25 when both protective caps are displaced at least 6 mm; 0.5 when the spike is also seated 23-25 mm with its collar at the port mouth; 1.0 when the marked axial liquid length is 15-27 mm with chamber axis within 12 degrees of horizontal and its lower region at least 10 mm below the port, the bag remains within tray bounds, both TCPs are at least 4 cm from chamber and port and within 5 cm of their starts, and bag and set rest for 1 s. All other outcomes score the highest completed uncontaminated stage.
reset_notes: Use a fresh sealed 500 mL bag and a fresh sterile giving set for each real trial; discard any item whose exposed spike or open port touched a glove, gripper or work surface. Place the bag at (0.32,0.06), ports toward the right arm. Place the set at (0.42,-0.13) in the clean molded cradle with its navy spike cap and the bag's blue port cap fully attached, chamber empty and roller clamp closed. Simulation reset restores both cap seals, contamination latch, spike joint and liquid length. Use object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Approximate rigid-body model. Bag dimensions and 530 g mass are consistent with 500 mL saline. Both cap displacements and spike depth are geometric. A conservative swept-clearance proxy latches contamination if an exposed interface reaches a gripper TCP or the nonsterile tray; microscopic sterility and glove state are not simulated. Fluid dynamics are simplified: measured gripper compression produces continuous graduated axial liquid length only while the spike is locked, the chamber is within 12 degrees of horizontal and its lower region is at least 10 mm below the wetted port. Scoring uses measured compression and axial length, not squeeze count.
